newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends weaker but off lows after Aust CPI.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends weaker but off lows after Aust CPI.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed weaker on Wednesday, but off its lows, after Australian consumer price data came in right on expectations, dealers said.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6920/27 and at 68.78 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.6928/35 and 68.84 at the open.
"It drifted down on concerns that the CPI in Australia today would be on the softer side and would therefore mean we could see further rate cuts in Australia," said a chief bank dealer.
"But the CPI came in right on expectations."
Australian underlying inflation rose 0.4 percent in the March quarter.
The Australian currency dipped briefly to a low of around US$0.7745 before bouncing back on short covering.
"And it's held up quite well. As a consequence the Kiwi, which got down to 0.6919 given, recovered to 0.6928 paid and is closing right in the middle of its range," the chief dealer said.
The Kiwi's fortunes were seen very closely tied to the Aussie's performance in the short-term.
